# SSGOI setup guide for Next.js App Router

This is the complete SSGOI setup guide for Next.js App Router. SSGOI adds page
transitions without replacing your router, layouts, or page files.

Current version: `@ssgoi/core@7.5.0-beta.0` (npm tag `beta`). All `@ssgoi/*` packages release together.

## Using another framework?

| Framework | Guide | Framework | Guide |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| React Router | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/frameworks/react-router.txt | Remix | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/frameworks/remix.txt |
| TanStack Router | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/frameworks/tanstack-router.txt | SvelteKit | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/frameworks/sveltekit.txt |
| Vue Router | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/frameworks/vue-router.txt | Nuxt | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/frameworks/nuxt.txt |
| Solid Router | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/frameworks/solid-router.txt | SolidStart | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/frameworks/solidstart.txt |
| Qwik City | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/frameworks/qwik.txt | Angular | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/frameworks/angular.txt |
| Expo Router | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/frameworks/expo.txt | | |

## 1. Install and add the provider

```bash
npm install @ssgoi/react@7.5.0-beta.0
```

```tsx
// app/ssgoi-provider.tsx
"use client";

import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { usePathname, useSelectedLayoutSegments } from "next/navigation";
import { Ssgoi, SsgoiLayoutBoundary, type SsgoiFramework } from "@ssgoi/react";
import { drill } from "@ssgoi/react/view-transitions";

const config = {
  transitions: [{ on: "/**", except: "/", transition: drill() }],
};

const INTERCEPTION_PREFIX = /^(?:\(\.\.\.\)|\(\.\.\)|\(\.\))+/;

const framework: SsgoiFramework = {
  useRoute: () => {
    const pathname = usePathname();
    // The page the children slot renders. During a soft intercept it is still
    // the background page, so no background boundary moves.
    const segments = useSelectedLayoutSegments();
    if (pathname == null) return null;
    const renderedPath = `/${segments
      .filter((segment) => !(segment.startsWith("(") && segment.endsWith(")")))
      .map((segment) => segment.replace(INTERCEPTION_PREFIX, ""))
      .filter(Boolean)
      .join("/")}`;
    return { pathname, renderedPath };
  },
};

export function SsgoiProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <main style={{ position: "relative", zIndex: 0, minHeight: "100dvh", overflowX: "clip" }}>
      <Ssgoi config={config} framework={framework}>
        <SsgoiLayoutBoundary>{children}</SsgoiLayoutBoundary>
      </Ssgoi>
    </main>
  );
}
```

In app/layout.tsx, wrap the existing `{children}` with `<SsgoiProvider>` inside
`<body>`. `SsgoiLayoutBoundary` takes no props. Keep the first one in the same
layout as `<Ssgoi>`: it reads the route for every boundary inside it, and
`renderedPath` is relative to that layout.

## 2. Route rules

`config.transitions` is a list of rules. Each rule names a navigation
relationship, the `transition` it plays, and which way is forward:

| Rule | Forward | Backward |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on` (+ optional `except`) | entering the scope | leaving the scope |
| `from` / `to` | `from` → `to` as written | the reverse (unless `bidirectional: false`) |
| `ordered: [...]` | increasing index | decreasing index |

`on`, `except`, `from` and `to` take one pattern or an array. `/posts` matches
exactly `/posts`; `/posts/*` exactly one more segment (`/posts/42`);
`/posts/**` `/posts` and every descendant. When several rules match, higher
`priority` (default 0) wins, then the more specific path, then declaration
order. Browser Back/Forward replay the effect recorded for that history entry
in reverse; a fresh link or `router.push` matches the current rules. Rules may
also be a function, `({ isMobile }) => rules`, for per-device motion.

```ts
import { drill, sheet, slide, zoom, fade } from "@ssgoi/react/view-transitions";

const config = {
  transitions: [
    { on: "/posts/**", except: "/posts", transition: drill() }, // list → detail
    { ordered: ["/home", "/search", "/profile"], transition: slide() }, // tabs
    { on: "/compose", transition: sheet({ type: "blur" }) }, // temporary task
    { from: "/gallery", to: "/photo/*", transition: zoom() }, // needs zoom markup
    { priority: -100, on: "/**", transition: fade() }, // fallback for the rest
  ],
};
```

## 3. Place boundaries by route structure

A boundary has two values: `key` decides when its DOM is replaced, and `id` is
the route SSGOI matches rules against. The id is always the route path. The key
comes from `config.layouts`: a boundary at depth N (the number of boundaries
above it) keys by the scope that matches at depth N, else by the route path.
Without `layouts`, the single boundary from step 1 replaces the page each time.

`layouts` is a tree of `{ paths, except?, layouts? }` using the rule patterns
above. Siblings are first-match; `layouts` is the next depth inside a scope; a
`*` or `:id` segment makes each captured value its own instance
(`/projects/:id/**`: one shell per project). Mirror your layout files:

```text
app/ssgoi-provider.tsx              <Ssgoi> + boundary (step 1)       depth 0
app/(top-level)/layout.tsx          boundary + <BottomNav /> outside  depth 1
app/(top-level)/posts, pinterest, profile/page.tsx
app/(top-level)/shop/layout.tsx     header + category tabs + boundary depth 2
app/(detail)/layout.tsx             boundary                          depth 1
app/(detail)/posts/[id], pinterest/[id], profile/[id]/page.tsx
```

```ts
const TOP_LEVEL = ["/posts", "/shop/**", "/pinterest", "/profile"];

const config = {
  layouts: [
    { paths: TOP_LEVEL, layouts: [{ paths: "/shop/**" }] },
    { paths: "/**", except: TOP_LEVEL },
  ],
  transitions: [{ from: TOP_LEVEL, to: TOP_LEVEL, transition: fade() } /* , step 2 rules */],
};
```

```tsx
// app/(top-level)/layout.tsx — (detail) and shop layouts wrap a boundary the same way
export default function TopLevelLayout({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <>
      <SsgoiLayoutBoundary>{children}</SsgoiLayoutBoundary>
      <BottomNav />
    </>
  );
}
```

Tab → tab keeps the depth-0 key, so only tab content moves and the nav stays.
Category → category keeps depths 0 and 1, so only depth 2 slides. Tab → detail
changes the depth-0 key, so the whole tab shell leaves, nav included. Use
`/shop/**`, not `/shop/*`: a `*` makes each category its own instance.

Intercepted modals need no setup: during a soft intercept the URL becomes the
modal's while `renderedPath` stays the background, so nothing behind it moves.
Render the `{modal}` slot outside the boundaries. Your app still owns the
`@modal` route files, `default.tsx`, and any middleware/proxy rewrites.

## 4. Pick an effect (all from `@ssgoi/react/view-transitions`)

- `drill()`: list → detail, hierarchical depth (`on` + `except`).
- `slide()`: tabs or ordered horizontal steps (`ordered`).
- `axis()`: sibling pages with Material shared-axis motion (`ordered`).
- `sheet()`: compose, filters, temporary tasks (`on`).
- `zoom()` / `hero()`: a card or image expands into its detail, or a shared
  object moves across two pages (`from` / `to`, element markup required).
- `scroll()`: vertical full-page sequence on web (`ordered`).
- `fade()`: quiet fade-through; a good low-priority fallback.
- `film()`, `strip()`, `rotate()`, `jaemin()`: expressive page swaps.

## 5. Verify and avoid common mistakes

Verify: a link animates the new page in and browser Back animates it out; with a
persistent shell, tab changes keep the header and nav still.

- Use `overflow-x: clip`, not `hidden`, on the element around `<Ssgoi>`: `hidden`
  makes it the scroll container. Keep `position: relative` and `z-index: 0`.
- Keep exactly one `<Ssgoi>` above both routes; do not nest providers.
- `SsgoiLayoutBoundary` throws if `<Ssgoi>` has no `framework`.
- Define `config` and `framework` at module scope: a new object every render
  rebuilds the engine and loses saved scroll positions.
- No animation: the boundary key must change and one rule must match the pair.
  Wrong region: keep persistent UI outside the inner boundary whose key changes.
